entry.title: 🚀 How Much Faster Does Your Site Load If You Compress Images?
entry.summary:
I used to obsess over shaving 10KB from my JavaScript bundle. Then I looked at my images. Ouch. Turns out, uncompressed images are silent killers for performance. They look fine, but they weigh more than the rest of your site combined. So I did a quick test to see how much difference compression actually makes. Spoiler: it’s not subtle. A landing page with 6 hero images and 12 thumbnails
Each image: ~500KB (mix of JPEGs + PNGs)
Total page weight: ~6.8 MB
Tested with Lighthouse on a throttled 4G connection. First Contentful Paint (FCP): 4.3s
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): 6.2s
Total Page Size: ~6.8 MB
Result: “Cool, I’ll go grab a coffee while this loads.” Ran all images through a compressor (👋 shameless plug: tinyimage.online). Hero images dropped to ~120KB each
Thumbnails to ~30KB
Total page weight: ~1.1 MB
New numbers: FCP: 1.2s
LCP: 1.8s
Total Page Size: ~1.1 MB
Result: “Oh hey, it’s already there.” Page size reduced by 84%
Load time cut by 70%
Lighthouse score: 56 → 93
That’s not a micro-optimization. That’s night-and-day. Google cares → Core Web Vitals directly impact SEO.
Users care → most people bounce if they wait more than 3 seconds.
You should care → faster pages = happier users + better ad revenue.
And honestly? Watching that Lighthouse dial swing from red to green feels better than any framework upgrade. Next time you’re sweating over webpack configs or debating which state management library to use… stop. Compress your images first. It’s the fastest performance win you’ll ever get. If you need a quick start: tinyimage.online. Drag, drop, done ✅. That’s it. Small tweak. Huge payoff.

entry.title: Overview of Trademark Registration for Position Mark
entry.summary: Over the last few years, trademark registration for the position marks has acquired a lot of recognition globally, especially in industries such as fashion, footwear, cosmetics, automobiles and electronics. For such types of businesses, protecting a unique placement helps build consumer trust and prevents competitors from creating confusingly similar products. Thus, to register a position mark is not only about a legal safeguard but also a strategic tool for strengthening brand identity and ensuring long-term market differentiation worldwide. A position mark is a type of trademark that protects the placement of a symbol, design or logo on a product. Unlike regular trademarks, which cover words, symbols or graphics in general, a position mark specifically secures the unique location of the mark. For example: The placement of three stripes on the side of a shoe. A logo always appears on the left chest side of a t-shirt. A distinct design consistently placed on a cosmetic product’s cap. These placements become identifiers of the brand. Customers see the position and instantly connect it to the company. In this sense, a position mark doesn’t just protect a design; it protects the way the design is used to signal brand authenticity.
